title: Excavation Competent Person: What They Must Do
summary: Trench work depends on a competent person who can spot hazards and has the authority to fix them fast. Know what they check, and know that they can pull you out of the trench.
talking_points: A competent person can identify existing and predictable hazards and working conditions that are unsanitary, hazardous, or dangerous, and has authority to take prompt action to eliminate them.
They determine the cave-in potential and whether shoring or another protective system is needed.
They classify soil and rock, by visual analysis and testing, and re-classify when conditions change.
They decide the slope of an excavation so it will not collapse from loads such as stored material, operating equipment, adjacent structures, or traffic, and make sure that slope is achieved.
They monitor water removal equipment and inspect excavations exposed to runoff from heavy rain to decide if diversion ditches, dikes, or other protection are needed.
They examine damaged protective system material or equipment to decide if it can still be used.
They can order workers out of the hazardous area right away when there is evidence of a possible cave-in, protective system failure, a hazardous atmosphere, or other hazardous conditions.
They design structural ramps used only by workers for getting in and out. Ramps for equipment must be designed by a competent person qualified in structural design.
site_hazards_to_check: No competent person named for the excavation
Signs of a possible cave-in, such as cracks or sloughing
Protective system parts that are bent, cracked, or damaged
Water removal equipment running with no one monitoring it
Runoff from heavy rain reaching the excavation
Stored material, equipment, or traffic close enough to load the trench walls
Homemade ramps used for getting in and out
discussion_questions: Who is the competent person on this job today, and how do we reach them?
What would make you stop work and get out of the trench right now?
What has changed since the last inspection that they need to see?
